title: Millimeter-wave spectrum of 2-propanimine
question: Measure the high-resolution millimeter-wave rotational spectrum of 2-propanimine in the laboratory and search for its emission in Sgr B2(N1S) and IRAS 16293B using ALMA spectral line surveys.

data.sensitivity: ReMoCA: 0.35 to 1.1 mJy beam−1 (median 0.8 mJy beam−1) per channel; PILS: 4–5 mJy beam−1 km s−1

what.value: LTE parameters and column densities for methanimine (CH2NH) and (E)/(Z)-1-propanimine toward Sgr B2(N1S)

evidence.quote: In order to search for 2-propanimine, CH3C(NH)CH3, toward Sgr B2(N1S), we relied on the LTE parameters that we previously derived for methanimine, CH2NH, toward this position with the ReMoCA survey (Margulès et al. 2022).

We recall in Table 6 the column density of methanimine and the upper limit to the column densities of the Z and E conformers of 1-propanimine that we derived earlier with the ReMoCA survey toward Sgr B2(N1S) (Margulès et al. 2022).

what.value: Methanimine (CH2NH) column density of 6–10×10^14 cm^-2 toward IRAS 16293B

evidence.quote: Toward this position methanimine CH2NH was detected as part of PILS by Ligterink et al. (2018) with a column density of 6–10×1014 cm−2 for excitation temperatures between 70 and 120 K.

what.value: List of identified molecules included in the complete LTE model of Sgr B2(N1S)

evidence.quote: The molecules included in the complete model comprise in particular those listed in Belloche et al. (2013).

recipe.goal: Perform quantum chemical calculations of 2-propanimine structure, dipole moments, vibrational frequencies, and internal rotation barriers
recipe.method: Geometry optimization in Cs symmetry, harmonic/anharmonic vibrational frequency calculations, and 1D/2D potential energy surface (PES) scans using DFT (B3LYP, M062X, MN15) and ab initio MP2 methods
key_parameters: DFT methods B3LYP, M062X, MN15 with 6-311++G(3df,3pd) basis set; MP2 with aug-cc-pVTZ basis set; 2D PES with B3LYP/6-311+g(2d,2p) in 2° steps from 0° to 120°
assumptions: Cs molecular symmetry for equilibrium geometry optimization (relaxed during PES scans)

recipe.goal: Synthesize 2-propanimine, measure laboratory millimeter-wave spectrum, and fit spectroscopic constants and internal rotation parameters
recipe.method: Synthesize sample from KOH and 2-amino-2-methylpropanenitrile, record absorption spectrum from 50 to 500 GHz, remove standing-wave baseline via Fourier transform, fit line peaks with second-derivative Voigt profiles, and iteratively assign and fit torsional-rotational transitions using Watson's A reduction Hamiltonian in Ir representation
key_parameters: Frequency ranges: 50–110 GHz, 150–330 GHz, 360–500 GHz; cell pressure 8–20 µBar at −60 °C; frequency uncertainties 25–200 kHz; 9,349 line frequencies (27,259 transitions) fitted with 44 parameters in ERHAM
assumptions: Partially resolved 14N quadrupole hyperfine components (~1% of lines) are replaced by their intensity-weighted average frequencies; two methyl tops treated as independent in BARRIER calculation

recipe.goal: Generate rotational line catalog and partition functions for astronomical searches
recipe.method: Predict transition frequencies and intensities up to J'' = 80 and 1 THz from the best-fit ERHAM parameters and MP2 dipole moments, and compute the torsional-rotational partition function by direct summation of Boltzmann factors up to J'' = 120
key_parameters: J'' up to 80 and frequency up to 1 THz for catalog; J'' up to 120 for partition function; µa = 1.3711 D, µb = −2.0643 D; reduced spin weight 2:2:2:1:1 (total 8) vs full spin weight 16:16:16:8:8 (total 64)
assumptions: Vibrational partition function estimated from harmonic/anharmonic vibrational energies in Table B5; no conformational correction needed (Fconf = 1.00)

recipe.goal: Search for 2-propanimine and derive column density upper limit toward Sgr B2(N1S) using ALMA ReMoCA data
recipe.method: Compute LTE synthetic spectra with Weeds using the ERHAM spectroscopic predictions and LTE parameters adopted from methanimine, compare with the observed ReMoCA spectrum and complete multi-molecule model toward Sgr B2(N1S), and derive a column density upper limit
key_parameters: θs = 2.0'', Trot = 230 K, ∆V = 5.0 km s−1, Voff = 0.0 km s−1 (Vsys = 62 km s−1), Fvib = 3.33, Fconf = 1.00
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) justified by high density (> 1×10^7 cm^-3); resolved emission size fixed to 2''; identical LTE parameters (θs, Trot, ∆V, Voff) to methanimine

recipe.goal: Search for 2-propanimine and derive column density upper limit toward IRAS 16293B using ALMA PILS data
recipe.method: Compute LTE synthetic spectra assuming optically thin emission using custom PILS routines and compare predicted bright transitions against line-free regions of the observed ALMA Band 7 spectrum down to the RMS noise level
key_parameters: Trot = 100 K, RMS noise level 4–5 mJy beam−1 km s−1, key frequency windows around 341.96, 346.86, and 361.34 GHz
assumptions: Optically thin emission and LTE at excitation temperature of 100 K

score_reason: The laboratory spectroscopy analysis is exceptionally reproducible with all XIAM/ERHAM input/output files, modified executables, and final catalogs publicly archived on Zenodo, CDS, and LSD. The ALMA upper limit derivations use public archival data and clearly stated LTE parameters for Sgr B2(N1S), though full reproduction from raw visibilities requires external survey reduction recipes (Belloche et al. 2019; Jørgensen et al. 2016) and the full Sgr B2(N1S) background line model.
rediscovery_reason: Both the spectroscopic input/output datasets (on Zenodo/CDS) and the ALMA datasets (in the ALMA archive, plus published PILS cubes) are public, and all main results (spectroscopic constants, partition functions, and column density upper limits) are quantitative.
